intro.text: As used in this Annual Report, references to the “Company,” “we,” “us,” or “our” refer to Kingstone Companies, Inc. (the “Holding Company”) and its subsidiaries. We offer property and casualty insurance products through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Kingstone Insurance Company (“KICO”). KICO is a New York domiciled carrier writing business through retail and wholesale agents and brokers. KICO is actively writing personal lines and commercial auto insurance in New York, and in 2024 was the 12th largest writer of homeowners insurance in New York. KICO is also licensed in the states of New Jersey, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Pennsylvania, New Hampshire, and Maine. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, 98.0% and 96.0% of KICO’s direct written premiums came from the New York policies.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Approximately 98% of our revenue during the year ended December 31, 2025 was derived from sources located in the State of New York and, accordingly, is affected by the prevailing regulatory, economic, legislative, demographic, competitive and other conditions in the state.
As a holding company with limited operations of our own, currently the principal sources of our funds are dividends and other payments from KICO.
Consequently, we must rely on KICO for our ability to repay debts, pay expenses and pay cash dividends to our stockholders.
Some of these systems rely on third-party vendors, through either a connection to, or an integration with, those third-parties’ systems.
We rely on our information technology, including artificial intelligence, and telecommunication systems, and the failure of these systems could materially and adversely affect our business.
We rely on these systems to support our operations.
The primary source of cash flow for the Holding Company are dividends and distributions received from KICO, which are subject to statutory restrictions.

Therefore, we cannot rely on the controls within these systems, including automated and manual process level controls, and remaining information technology general controls, that are dependent upon the information derived from such systems.
